error.message: invalid structural ResultPackage: RUN-110-001-DISPATCH references unknown acceptance criteria: TASK-110

instructions: Complete the original TASK-110 implementation from failed_head_sha without widening scope or changing TASK semantics.

Correct the structural ResultPackage completion contract: every claims[].satisfies entry must reference only actual TASK-110 acceptance criterion IDs AC1 through AC11; TASK-110 itself is not an acceptance criterion.
Do not retry, reroute, push, merge, or introduce worker-side lineage, sandbox, mutation-capability, review, or publication authority beyond TASK-110.

acceptance.condition: The checked-in dependency pin and launcher provenance authority both identify exactly AIOS-renew commit b5ce283232587c66144a68f842e3b196d7cf2601, and regression coverage proves the previous worker kernel is rejected as stale.

A valid worker runtime for the new immutable pin is reused, while an older or unverifiable runtime is deterministically rebuilt through the existing single dedicated worker-runtime path without creating another runtime or state store.
Codex RUN delegates to the pinned AIOS-renew run command with TASK, executor, and repository context only and no obsolete worker-owned Codex sandbox, permission, or mutation-capability argument.
Antigravity RUN uses the same semantic command contract as Codex RUN and differs only by the surface-bound executor identity, with no worker-side retry or reroute.

Codex and Antigravity FIX surfaces require an explicit finding identifier, and one accepted FIX request delegates exactly once to AIOS-renew remediation using the exact TASK, finding, executor, and repository values supplied by the surface.

The active FIX path does not resolve local REVIEW/REMEDIATION lineage, infer a finding, inspect current HEAD to select a finding, or pass local REVIEW, REMEDIATION, prior-review, sandbox, scope, or verification authority to the kernel.

A FIX request without a finding fails closed before kernel invocation, and an AIOS-renew remote-lineage failure is surfaced without worker-side retry, fallback, artifact reconstruction, or Executor substitution.
STATUS remains read-only and does not resolve remediation lineage, sample implementation HEAD for remediation selection, invoke an Executor, or publish.

Active Codex and Antigravity documentation consistently shows `$aios-worker FIX TASK-N FINDING-ID` and `/aios-renew-worker FIX TASK-N FINDING-ID`, documents the exact immutable kernel pin, and retains review-before-publication and namespace isolation.
Existing RUN/FIX post-PASS behavior still reports the review candidate for ChatGPT semantic review and performs zero automatic push, merge, semantic review, or publication.

Regression tests prove the new pin/provenance contract, stale-runtime rebuild, sandbox-free RUN delegation, explicit-finding FIX translation, zero local-lineage authority in the active FIX path, missing-finding failure, one kernel invocation, STATUS safety, executor-surface identity isolation, and zero pre-review push.

assumptions: The approved AIOS-renew consumer kernel for this synchronization is exactly b5ce283232587c66144a68f842e3b196d7cf2601.
Immutable source+commit pinning, PEP 610 provenance validation, dedicated worker-runtime bootstrap, and stale-runtime replacement remain authoritative.
AIOS-renew now resolves Codex and Antigravity mutation capability before the native Executor invocation; the worker must not independently select native sandbox or permission policy.
AIOS-renew now supports canonical remote remediation execution from TASK, finding identifier, selected Executor, and repository location without local REVIEW/REMEDIATION artifact paths.
Human execution authorization, ChatGPT semantic review, and guarded publication after semantic PASS remain unchanged.

hard: The active immutable dependency pin and launcher provenance authority must identify exactly AIOS-renew commit b5ce283232587c66144a68f842e3b196d7cf2601. The worker must not track a moving branch or accept another source/commit as authoritative.

Existing PEP 610 source+commit provenance validation and atomic stale-runtime replacement must remain fail closed; a runtime pinned to the previous worker kernel must be treated as stale and rebuilt before dispatch.

RUN must preserve the exact Human task identifier and selected surface executor and delegate to the pinned AIOS-renew run boundary without adding worker-owned Codex sandbox, permission, or mutation-capability arguments.

FIX must require one explicit Human-supplied finding identifier in addition to the task identifier. The worker must preserve that exact finding value and delegate through the pinned AIOS-renew remediation boundary using finding-based canonical remote lineage resolution.

The active FIX path must not require, select, infer, materialize, or pass local REVIEW, REMEDIATION, prior-review, reviewed-SHA, modification-scope, or affected-verification inputs solely to reconstruct canonical remediation lineage.
The worker must not choose a finding from current HEAD, local artifacts, branch ordering, timestamps, latest/newest heuristics, or any semantic inference.

Codex and Antigravity must expose the same semantic RUN/FIX/STATUS protocol; their only execution difference is the executor identity fixed by the separate surface. Codex remains $aios-worker and Antigravity remains /aios-renew-worker.

FIX surface syntax must make the finding explicit, for example `FIX TASK-N FINDING-ID`; omission of the finding must fail before kernel invocation rather than falling back to the legacy inferred/local-lineage path.

Each admitted RUN or FIX request may invoke the pinned AIOS-renew kernel at most once. Worker parsing, bootstrap, provenance, or kernel failure must not cause retry, reroute, fallback, or invocation of another Executor.
STATUS remains read-only for product implementation, executor authority, publication, and remediation lineage and must not invoke an Executor.
Successful RUN/FIX continues to leave the implementation commit local for independent ChatGPT semantic review and performs zero worker-side push or merge.
The retired Antigravity /aios-worker workflow remains inactive and must not be modified into an alternate active execution surface.
Do not push from executor execution.

task.goal: Synchronize the repository-owned Codex and Antigravity worker surfaces with the currently approved AIOS-renew kernel, preserving the immutable pinned-runtime model while making the worker a thinner deterministic UI: RUN and STATUS must delegate without worker-owned native capability selection, and FIX must carry one explicit Human-supplied finding identifier into AIOS-renew remote canonical remediation resolution instead of resolving REVIEW/REMEDIATION lineage locally.
non_goals: Modify AIOS-renew source code or replace its immutable contracts.
Modify Product Intelligence, entity resolution, marketplace adapters, browser automation, scoring, ranking, ingestion, Drive, or other product behavior.
Follow AIOS-renew main, a tag, or any moving ref automatically at runtime.
Add automatic kernel upgrades, polling, watchers, queues, or background synchronization.
Add retry, reroute, fallback, executor substitution, planner, router, or second execution authority.
Allow the worker to infer a remediation finding when the Human did not supply one.
Recreate remote REVIEW/REMEDIATION lineage resolution in the worker.
Change REVIEW, REMEDIATION, affected-verification, DELTA-review, or publication semantics.
Add worker-side push, merge, semantic review, or publication.
task.problem: The active Python Agent worker launcher still pins an older AIOS-renew commit, performs local REVIEW/REMEDIATION discovery for FIX, and adds a Codex sandbox argument that the current kernel no longer exposes because mutation capability is now resolved inside AIOS Runtime. The current approved kernel at b5ce283232587c66144a68f842e3b196d7cf2601 already owns remote canonical remediation lineage resolution through an explicit finding identifier and owns native mutation-capability selection. Keeping the old worker behavior duplicates deterministic authority and can make the worker command surface incompatible with the pinned kernel. The worker must be synchronized without following a moving branch or becoming a second orchestration layer.
